key_big: A square root uses two equal factors; a cube root uses three. √36 = 6 (not 18) and 2³ = 8 (not 6).
key_sub: To estimate a square root, find the perfect squares on each side: 49 < 50 < 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8, about 7.1. The side of a square is the square root of its area; the edge of a cube is the cube root of its volume.
body_html:
Perfect squares and square roots

A perfect square is a whole number times itself. 7 × 7 = 49, so 49 is a perfect square. We write 72 = 49 and say “7 squared”. It is the area of a square with sides of 7.

The square root undoes squaring. √49 = 7, because 72 = 49.

Estimating a square root

When a number is not a perfect square, find the perfect squares on each side of it. Its root is between their roots.

Example 1

Estimate √30 to one decimal place.

52 = 25 and 62 = 36, so √30 is between 5 and 6, a little closer to 5. Try 5.42 = 29.16 and 5.52 = 30.25. 30 is closer to 30.25.

Answer: √30 ≈ 5.5

Perfect cubes and cube roots

A perfect cube is a whole number used as a factor three times. 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so 27 is a perfect cube. We write 33 = 27 and say “3 cubed”. It is the volume of a cube with edges of 3.

The cube root undoes cubing. ∛27 = 3, because 33 = 27.

Example 2

A cube-shaped box has a volume of 64 cm3. How long is each edge?

Edge × edge × edge = 64. 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so the edge is ∛64.

Answer: 4 cm

Example 3

What is (−2)3?

(−2) × (−2) = 4, then 4 × (−2) = −8. Three negative factors give a negative answer. So ∛(−8) = −2.

Answer: −8

faq.q: What is the difference between a square root and a cube root?
faq.a: A square root uses two equal factors and a cube root uses three. √64 = 8 because 8 × 8 = 64, and ∛64 = 4 because 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.

faq.q: How do you estimate √50 without a calculator?
faq.a: Find the perfect squares on each side: 7 × 7 = 49 and 8 × 8 = 64. So √50 is between 7 and 8 and very close to 7, about 7.1.

faq.q: What do Grade 8 students learn about squares and cubes in BC?
faq.a: In the BC Grade 8 curriculum (Number), students work with perfect squares and cubes and with square and cube roots, and use them to find the side of a square or the edge of a cube.

faq.q: What are the perfect cubes from 1 to 1000?

items.q: What is 9<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 92 means 9 × 9 = 81. It is not 9 × 2 = 18.

items.q: What is 11<sup>2</sup>?
What is 12<sup>2</sup>?
What is 13<sup>2</sup>?
What is 15<sup>2</sup>?
Which perfect square does this square array show?
items.e: The array has 6 rows of 6 tiles: 6 × 6 = 62 = 36 tiles. 12 is only the rows plus the columns, and 20 is only the tiles around the border.

items.q: Which perfect square does this square array show?
items.e: The array has 8 rows of 8 tiles: 8 × 8 = 82 = 64 tiles. 16 is only the rows plus the columns, and 28 is only the tiles around the border.

items.q: Which number is a perfect square?
items.e: 12 × 12 = 144, so 144 is a perfect square. 112 = 121 and 132 = 169, so the other numbers fall between perfect squares.

items.q: Which number is a perfect square?
items.e: 14 × 14 = 196, so 196 is a perfect square. 132 = 169 and 152 = 225, so the other numbers fall between perfect squares.

items.q: Which number is a perfect square?
items.e: 15 × 15 = 225, so 225 is a perfect square. 125 = 5 × 5 × 5 is a perfect cube, not a square.

items.q: Which number is a perfect square?
items.e: 20 × 20 = 400, so 400 is a perfect square. 40 and 4000 are not squares: a perfect square ending in 0 needs an even number of zeros (100, 400, 2500).

items.q: Which number is not a perfect square?
items.e: 49 = 72, 64 = 82, 36 = 62. 72 = 49 and 82 = 64, so 50 is between two perfect squares and is not one itself.

items.q: Which number is not a perfect square?
items.e: 100 = 102, 121 = 112, 169 = 132. 142 = 196 and 152 = 225, so 200 is between two perfect squares and is not one itself.

items.q: Which is the same as 7<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: The small 2 tells how many 7s to multiply: 72 = 7 × 7 = 49. 7 × 2 and 7 + 7 both give 14.

items.q: What is 20<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 202 = 20 × 20 = 400. Think 2 × 2 = 4, then add two zeros, one for each 20. 40 is 20 × 2.

items.q: What is 30<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 302 = 30 × 30 = 900. Think 3 × 3 = 9, then add two zeros, one for each 30. 60 is 30 × 2.

items.q: What is the next perfect square: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …?
items.e: These are 12, 22, 32, 42 and 52. The next one is 62 = 36. The gaps are 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next gap is 11.

items.q: How many perfect squares are between 50 and 100?
items.e: 72 = 49 is too small and 102 = 100 is not between 50 and 100. Only 82 = 64 and 92 = 81 fit: 2 perfect squares.

items.q: A square array has 7 rows of 7 tiles. How many tiles must be added to make the next square array, 8 rows of 8 tiles?
items.e: 82 − 72 = 64 − 49 = 15 tiles: one new row of 8 and one new column of 7. Adding only one row (8) leaves a rectangle.

items.q: Which perfect square is closest to 90?
items.e: 92 = 81 and 102 = 100. 90 − 81 = 9 and 100 − 90 = 10, so 81 is closer, but only by 1.

items.q: What is √36?
What is √64?
What is √81?
items.e: 9 × 9 = 81, so √81 = 9. Check by squaring: 92 = 81.

items.q: What is √121?
items.e: 11 × 11 = 121, so √121 = 11. Check by squaring: 112 = 121.

items.q: What is √144?
What is √169?
items.e: 13 × 13 = 169, so √169 = 13. Check by squaring: 132 = 169.

items.q: What is √225?
items.e: 15 × 15 = 225, so √225 = 15. Check by squaring: 152 = 225.

items.q: What is √400?
√50 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect squares on each side: 72 = 49 and 82 = 64. 50 is between them, so √50 is between 7 and 8 (√50 ≈ 7.07).

items.q: √20 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect squares on each side: 42 = 16 and 52 = 25. 20 is between them, so √20 is between 4 and 5 (√20 ≈ 4.47).

items.q: √30 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect squares on each side: 52 = 25 and 62 = 36. 30 is between them, so √30 is between 5 and 6 (√30 ≈ 5.48).

items.q: √70 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect squares on each side: 82 = 64 and 92 = 81. 70 is between them, so √70 is between 8 and 9 (√70 ≈ 8.37).

items.q: √110 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect squares on each side: 102 = 100 and 112 = 121. 110 is between them, so √110 is between 10 and 11 (√110 ≈ 10.49).

items.q: Which point is closest to √50 on the number line?
items.e: 72 = 49 and 82 = 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8. 50 is closer to 49, so √50 is closer to 7. √50 ≈ 7.07, so the answer is point C.

items.q: Which point is closest to √10 on the number line?
items.e: 32 = 9 and 42 = 16, so √10 is between 3 and 4. 10 is closer to 9, so √10 is closer to 3. √10 ≈ 3.16, so the answer is point B.

items.q: Which point is closest to √80 on the number line?
items.e: 82 = 64 and 92 = 81, so √80 is between 8 and 9. 80 is closer to 81, so √80 is closer to 9. √80 ≈ 8.94, so the answer is point D.

items.q: Estimate √50 to one decimal place.
items.e: 72 = 49 and 82 = 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8. √50 ≈ 7.071, so to one decimal place √50 ≈ 7.1. Halving gives 25, but 252 = 625.

items.q: Estimate √20 to one decimal place.
items.e: 42 = 16 and 52 = 25, so √20 is between 4 and 5. √20 ≈ 4.472, so to one decimal place √20 ≈ 4.5. 4.4 comes from 20 − 16 = 4. That is not how roots work: 4.42 = 19.36 and 4.52 = 20.25.

items.q: Estimate √90 to one decimal place.
items.e: 92 = 81 and 102 = 100, so √90 is between 9 and 10. √90 ≈ 9.487, so to one decimal place √90 ≈ 9.5. 9.4 cuts off the digits instead of rounding: 9.48… rounds up to 9.5.

items.q: What is √36 + √64?
items.e: Find each root first: √36 = 6 and √64 = 8, so √36 + √64 = 6 + 8 = 14. You cannot add under the root sign: √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 is a different number.

items.q: What is 2<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 23 means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. It is not 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: What is 3<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 33 means 3 × 3 × 3 = 27. It is not 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: What is 4<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 43 means 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. It is not 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: What is 5<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 53 means 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. It is not 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: What is 6<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 63 means 6 × 6 × 6 = 216. It is not 6 × 3 = 18.

items.q: What is 10<sup>3</sup>?
This large cube is built from small cubes. How many small cubes are in it?
items.e: There are 3 layers, and each layer has 3 × 3 = 9 small cubes. 3 × 9 = 33 = 27. 9 counts only one face, and 19 counts only the cubes you can see.

items.q: This large cube is built from small cubes. How many small cubes are in it?
items.e: There are 4 layers, and each layer has 4 × 4 = 16 small cubes. 4 × 16 = 43 = 64. 16 counts only one face, and 37 counts only the cubes you can see.

items.q: Which number is a perfect cube?
items.e: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so 125 is a perfect cube. 25 = 52 is a square, not a cube; 75 is between 43 = 64 and 53 = 125; 150 is between 53 = 125 and 63 = 216.

items.q: Which number is a perfect cube?
items.e: 6 × 6 × 6 = 216, so 216 is a perfect cube. 36 = 62 is a square, not a cube; 18 is between 23 = 8 and 33 = 27; 100 = 102 is a square, not a cube.

items.q: Which number is a perfect cube?
items.e: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000, so 1000 is a perfect cube. 100 = 102 is a square, not a cube; 300 is between 63 = 216 and 73 = 343; 30 is between 33 = 27 and 43 = 64.

items.q: Which number is a perfect cube?
items.e: 7 × 7 × 7 = 343, so 343 is a perfect cube. 49 = 72 is a square, not a cube; 21 is between 23 = 8 and 33 = 27; 147 is between 53 = 125 and 63 = 216.

items.q: Which number is not a perfect cube?
items.e: 1 = 13, 8 = 23 and 27 = 33. 9 = 32 is a perfect square, but 23 = 8 and 33 = 27, so 9 is not a cube.

items.q: Which number is both a perfect square and a perfect cube?
items.e: 64 = 8 × 8 and 64 = 4 × 4 × 4, so 64 is both. 16 is only a square, and 8 and 27 are only cubes.

items.q: Which is the same as 4<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: The small 3 tells how many 4s to multiply: 43 = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. 4 × 3 and 4 + 4 + 4 both give 12.

items.q: What is the volume of this cube?
items.e: Volume of a cube = edge × edge × edge = 7 × 7 × 7 = 343 cm3. 49 is the area of one face, and 294 = 6 × 49 is the surface area.

items.q: What is the next perfect cube: 1, 8, 27, 64, …?
items.e: These are 13, 23, 33 and 43. The next one is 53 = 125. 81 and 100 are perfect squares, not cubes.

items.q: What is 20<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 203 = 20 × 20 × 20 = 8000. Think 23 = 8, then add three zeros (one for each 20).

items.q: Which is greater: 2<sup>3</sup> or 3<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 23 = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 and 32 = 3 × 3 = 9. 9 > 8, so 32 is greater.

items.q: What is (−3)<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: (−3) × (−3) × (−3): the first two give +9, then 9 × (−3) = −27. Three negative factors give a negative answer.

items.q: What is ∛27?
items.e: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so ∛27 = 3. Dividing by 3 gives 9, but 9 × 9 × 9 = 729.

items.q: What is ∛64?
What is ∛125?
items.e: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so ∛125 = 5. 25 comes from 5 × 25 = 125, which uses only two factors.

items.q: What is ∛216?
items.e: 6 × 6 × 6 = 216, so ∛216 = 6. Dividing by 3 gives 72, but a cube root is not 216 ÷ 3.

items.q: What is ∛512?
items.e: 8 × 8 × 8 = 512, so ∛512 = 8. 64 is 82, not the cube root.

items.q: What is ∛729?
What is ∛1000?
Which statement is true?
items.e: 8 × 8 = 64, so √64 = 8. 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so ∛64 = 4. A cube root uses three equal factors, so it is smaller here.

items.q: What is ∛27 + ∛216?
items.e: Find each root first: ∛27 = 3 and ∛216 = 6, so 3 + 6 = 9. 243 adds the numbers under the roots, 81 divides each by 3 (9 + 72), and 18 multiplies 3 × 6.

items.q: ∛50 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect cubes on each side: 33 = 27 and 43 = 64. 50 is between them, so ∛50 is between 3 and 4 (∛50 ≈ 3.68). 7 and 8 would be for √50.

items.q: ∛80 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect cubes on each side: 43 = 64 and 53 = 125. 80 is between them, so ∛80 is between 4 and 5 (∛80 ≈ 4.31). 8 and 9 would be for √80.

items.q: ∛20 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect cubes on each side: 23 = 8 and 33 = 27. 20 is between them, so ∛20 is between 2 and 3 (∛20 ≈ 2.71). 4 and 5 would be for √20.

items.q: ∛300 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect cubes on each side: 63 = 216 and 73 = 343. 300 is between them, so ∛300 is between 6 and 7 (∛300 ≈ 6.69). 17 and 18 would be for √300.

items.q: ∛600 is between which two whole numbers?
items.e: Find the perfect cubes on each side: 83 = 512 and 93 = 729. 600 is between them, so ∛600 is between 8 and 9 (∛600 ≈ 8.43). 24 and 25 would be for √600.

items.q: What is ∛(−8)?
items.e: (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = 4 × (−2) = −8, so ∛(−8) = −2. A negative number has a cube root, because three negative factors give a negative product.

items.q: What is ∛(−64)?
The volume of this cube is 216 cm3. How long is each edge?
items.e: Edge × edge × edge = 216. 6 × 6 × 6 = 216, so each edge is ∛216 = 6 cm. 216 ÷ 6 = 36 shares the volume among the 6 faces, which does not give an edge.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: A cube root is the number used three times as a factor. 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so ∛125 = 5.

items.q: Which number has a whole-number cube root?
items.e: 7 × 7 × 7 = 343, so ∛343 = 7 and 343 is a perfect cube. 400 and 81 are perfect squares, not cubes, and 300 is between 63 = 216 and 73 = 343.

items.q: Which whole number is ∛30 closest to?
items.e: 33 = 27 and 43 = 64. 30 is much closer to 27, so ∛30 is closest to 3 (∛30 ≈ 3.11). 10 is 30 ÷ 3, and 5 is close to √30, the square root.

sets.title: Word problems: area of a square and volume of a cube

items.q: A square plot in a Surrey community garden has an area of 64 m<sup>2</sup>. How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 64. 8 × 8 = 64, so each side is √64 = 8 m. 16 = 64 ÷ 4 would come from a perimeter, not an area.

items.q: The floor of a square room in a Whistler cabin has an area of 30 m<sup>2</sup>. How long is each side, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
items.e: √30 ≈ 5.477. The hundredths digit is 7, so round up: 5.5 m. Check: 5.52 = 30.25, which is close to 30.

items.q: A square poster for the Terry Fox Run has an area of 3600 cm<sup>2</sup>. How long is each side?
For a school assembly in Burnaby, 169 chairs are set out in a square: the number of rows equals the number of chairs in each row. How many rows are there?
items.e: Rows × chairs per row = 169, and they are equal. 13 × 13 = 169, so there are 13 rows. Halving (84) or dividing by 4 (42) does not give a square root.

items.q: A square horse paddock in the Okanagan has an area of 900 m<sup>2</sup>. How much fencing goes all the way around it?
items.e: Each side is √900 = 30 m. A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 30 = 120 m. 30 m is only one side.

items.q: Chloe builds a square sandbox with an area of 5 m<sup>2</sup>. She has 9 m of cedar boards for the border. Is that enough?
items.e: Each side is √5 ≈ 2.236 m. The border is 4 × 2.236 ≈ 8.94 m, which is less than 9 m. Yes, it is enough. (4 × 5 = 20 uses the area as the side.)

items.q: A cube-shaped box holds exactly 1 litre, which is 1000 cm<sup>3</sup>. How long is each edge of the box?
items.e: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000, so each edge is ∛1000 = 10 cm. 31.6 is √1000, the square root, and 100 × 100 × 100 is far too big.

items.q: A cube-shaped storage box for hockey gear has edges of 40 cm. What is its volume?
items.e: 40 × 40 × 40 = 64 000 cm3. Think 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, then add three zeros. 1600 is the area of one face.

items.q: A salmon hatchery near the Fraser River has a cube-shaped tank with edges of 2 m. What is its volume?
items.e: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 m3. 2 × 3 = 6 is a common mistake, and 24 = 6 × 4 is the surface area.

items.q: Jasleen makes ice cubes that are 3 cm on each edge. What is the volume of one ice cube?
items.e: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm3. 9 is the area of one face, 54 = 6 × 9 is the surface area, and 36 = 12 × 3 is the total length of the 12 edges.

items.q: Ethan builds a large cube from small wooden cubes, with 5 small cubes along each edge. How many small cubes does he use?
items.e: 5 layers of 5 × 5 = 25 cubes: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 small cubes. 25 is only one layer.

items.q: A cube-shaped wooden planter has a volume of 125 000 cm<sup>3</sup>. How long is each edge?
items.e: 50 × 50 × 50 = 125 000, so each edge is 50 cm. ∛125 = 5, and each 0 in 50 gives three zeros in the volume. 500 × 500 × 500 = 125 000 000 is far too big.

items.q: Cube A has edges of 2 cm. Cube B has edges of 4 cm. How many times greater is the volume of cube B?
items.e: Cube A: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cm3. Cube B: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm3. 64 ÷ 8 = 8 times. Doubling the edge doubles each of the 3 factors: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

items.q: A square bathroom floor has an area of 16 m<sup>2</sup>. It is covered with square tiles that are 0.5 m on each side. How many tiles are in each row?
items.e: Each side of the floor is √16 = 4 m. 4 ÷ 0.5 = 8 tiles in each row (and 64 tiles in all).

items.q: An orchard in Kelowna plants 256 apple trees in a square: the number of rows equals the number of trees in each row. How many trees are in each row?
items.e: 16 × 16 = 256, so there are 16 trees in each row. 128 = 256 ÷ 2 and 64 = 256 ÷ 4 are not square roots.

items.q: Arjun has a square garden bed with sides of 3 m. He makes a new square bed with sides of 6 m. How many times greater is the area of the new bed?
items.e: Old bed: 3 × 3 = 9 m2. New bed: 6 × 6 = 36 m2. 36 ÷ 9 = 4 times. Doubling the side doubles both factors: 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: A cube-shaped tank on Vancouver Island collects rainwater. Its volume is 8 m<sup>3</sup>. How long is each edge?
items.e: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so each edge is ∛8 = 2 m. 4 is 8 ÷ 2, and 2.8 is close to √8, the square root.

items.q: A block of packed snow for a snow fort is a cube with edges of 30 cm. What is its volume?
items.e: 30 × 30 × 30 = 27 000 cm3. Think 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, then add three zeros. 900 is the area of one face.

items.q: A cube-shaped gift box has a volume of 90 cm<sup>3</sup>. Each edge is between which two lengths?
items.e: 43 = 64 and 53 = 125. 90 is between them, so each edge is between 4 cm and 5 cm (∛90 ≈ 4.48 cm). 9 and 10 would be for √90, the square root, and 30 is 90 ÷ 3.

items.q: Hana says a cube with edges of 2 cm has a volume of 6 cm<sup>3</sup>. Which statement is correct?
c: Hana is wrong. The volume is 4 cm<sup>3</sup>.
Hana is wrong. The volume is 24 cm<sup>3</sup>.
Hana is wrong. The volume is 8 cm<sup>3</sup>.
items.e: 23 means 2 × 2 × 2, not 2 × 3. The volume is 8 cm3. 4 is the area of one face and 24 is the surface area.
